provenance.carry_m: tuned on the development set: 3 m (cost 30) against 2 m (31 or more), as v1 found; for records of a junction's width or more
provenance.piece_carry_m: fixed by the label definitions: a curb cut or short piece lies along a way when most of it is within about 2 m
provenance.align_max_deg: fixed, as v1: a way crossing a record at more than 45 degrees there is not along it
provenance.follow_max_deg: tuned on the development set: 15 degrees (cost 30) against 10 or 20 (31 or more). The development labels cite a way for a piece at 0.9-10 degrees and not at 17 or more, with a few cited at 20-23 degrees
provenance.rival_extra_deg: not identified by the development set — 10 and 15 degrees gave the same result, 5 a worse one — so the selection rule's more conservative value: a second way within 30 degrees of the piece, along all of it, makes a corner
provenance.rival_share: fixed: 'along the whole piece' is 95% of its samples within piece_carry_m, allowing a sample of rounding at a quarter-metre spacing
provenance.end_slop_m: fixed by the label definitions: about a junction's width (5 m)
provenance.structure_min_m: fixed: a way tagged as the City's structure carries it from a metre; OSM splits stairs and bridges into pieces shorter than the end slop
provenance.cover_min: not identified by the development set — 0.6 and 0.75 gave the same result — so the selection rule's more conservative value
provenance.contest_margin_m: v1's value, never identified by a development set
provenance.contest_max: v1's value, never identified by a development set
provenance.short_piece_m: fixed by the label definitions: a junction's width
provenance.piece_carrier_share: fixed: a way the piece follows for a quarter of its length carries it, rather than touching its end
provenance.piece_cover_min: fixed as v1's coverage: the one way must carry most of the piece
provenance.curb_cover_min: fixed: the ways a curb cut follows must carry at least half of it
provenance.kerb_node_m: fixed by the label definitions: a kerb node within about 2 m
provenance.near_m: fixed by the label definitions: no counterpart within about 5 m
provenance.displaced_steps_m: fixed at the candidate radius, the most conservative value: the development set has one displaced stair (steps 7.5 m away) and cannot tell 10, 15 or 25 m apart

candidate_contract.fine_for: curb cuts and records shorter than a junction's width

development.selection_rule: Lowest development cost, where a false attachment — a partial or wrong set, a match where OSM has nothing, or a match where the labeller could not name the elements — costs 2 and an abstention or a miss on an obvious correspondence costs 1; then most exact sets; then the most conservative values: smaller follow angle, larger rival allowance, smaller carry distance, larger coverage.
development.what_it_is: Where matcher v2 was designed and tuned, including the PA-GEO-05 held-out records whose failures shaped it. Not a result.

candidate_generation.what_it_is: Every element an obvious label names, checked against v2's candidates for the record. An element no labeller named cannot be missed, so this is recall of the labelled correspondence, not of every possible one.

intervals_95.what_they_are: Sampling uncertainty over these records, conditional on the frozen labels. Not whether the labels are right, not field truth, not other places.

D_overlap_2m.ranks_ways_by: share of the record within 2 m (higher is better)

intervals_95.what_they_are: Sampling uncertainty over these records, conditional on the frozen labels. Not whether the labels are right, not field truth, not other places.

categories.curb_cut_continuation_under_a_quarter: Incomplete set, never a wrong element. The curb-cut piece lies along the end of a sidewalk and in line with the crossing it runs onto; the crossing is within 2 m of most of the piece but nearest to under a quarter of its samples, so the quarter-share carrier rule drops it. The kerb node and the sidewalk v2 names are the labelled ones; the crossing start is missing.
categories.perpendicular_touch_abstention: Safe direction. A curb cut or connector is touched at about 90 degrees by a sidewalk and OSM has nothing along it; the labeller says no counterpart. v2's junction rule counts any eligible way within 5 m, aligned or not, so it abstains instead of saying unmatched.
categories.follow_angle_boundary: Threshold boundary. The piece follows its way at 22-31 degrees (a bent footway, a median cut-through, a sidewalk start) and the labeller cited it; v2 requires 15 degrees and abstains. In one record the sidewalk is at 15.3 degrees and the crossing at 13.4, so v2 names the crossing.
categories.kerb_distance_boundary: Threshold boundary. A kerb node just beyond the 2 m definition: at 2.26 m the labeller cited it ('about 2 m') and v2 abstained; at 2.02 m the labeller counted a second kerb that v2 did not see, and v2 named the first.
categories.trail_on_service_ways: Representation question. OSM tags the trail's ways only highway=service; the labeller could not tell whether they are the same gravel trail or a service track. v2 lets a service way carry a trail, as v1 did.
categories.crossing_node_on_the_sidewalk_line: Representation v2 has no rule for. A City crossing of an alley where OSM runs the sidewalk straight across and marks the crossing with a highway=crossing node on it: the labeller cited the node (with the sidewalk once); v2 matches the sidewalk way that covers the record and names no node.
categories.stair_split_between_steps_and_footway: Over-commitment. A 6.9 m stair lies 2 m on OSM steps and 4.3 m on a plain footway; the labeller could not settle the split. v2's structure rule carries the steps piece from a metre and treats 4.3 m of footway as end slop.
categories.apex_ramp_serving_two_crossings: Over-commitment. A 0.6 m apex ramp serves both crosswalks; one kerb node lies within 2 m and the other 5.5 m away. v2 names the near one; the labeller could not tell which marks this ramp.
categories.piece_past_the_crossing_end: Over-commitment. The curb-cut piece continues the line of a crossing from 0.8 m past its end to a sidewalk it crosses at 84 degrees; v2 matches the crossing, the labeller saw no OSM way it overlaps.
categories.non_curb_piece_onto_a_crossing: Over-commitment. A 1.2 m junction piece, not a curb cut, straddles a sidewalk's end and the crossing's start in line; crossings carry only curb cuts and crossings, so the sidewalk claims all of it and no rival is seen.
categories.end_slop_boundary: Threshold boundary. A bridge record runs 5.5 m onto its approach, just past the 5 m end slop; the labeller treated it as end slop.
categories.offset_crossride: Neither side names elements. OSM's crossride lies parallel 6.5 m away; the labeller called it possibly the same crossing drawn offset, v2 finds nothing within 5 m and says unmatched.

repeat_labels.what_it_is: The same records labelled again by other AI instances of the same model from the same material: the consistency of this labelling procedure, not inter-rater reliability between independent people, and not accuracy.

full_pilot_dry_run.what_it_is: Matcher v2 run once over every eligible record, with matcher v1 beside it for the same records. Counts, sizes and time only: nothing here says a decision is right. The held-out benchmark is the measure.

curb_cuts_v1_matched_to_ways_only.what_it_is: The curb cuts PA-GEO-06 could not accept: matched by v1 to ways only, with no OSM kerb node. How v2 decides the same records.

potential_evidence.what_it_is: Research only. What a later, licensed reconciliation could compare: never routed, never called verified, and resting on correspondences the benchmark measured only on a sample.
potential_evidence.curb_ramps_whose_record_spans_over_20m_m: Long City records carrying CURBCUT = Y: the City does not say where along them the ramp is, so the extent is the record's own and locates no ramp.
